bull.b: A 10-year, $636M contracted expansion that yields roughly $51M average annual NOI materially converts development risk into long‑dated, tenant-backed cash flows. This durable contracted revenue supports predictable operating-lease income as capacity is delivered and scales over multiple years.

bull.t: Large Bitcoin treasury providing funding optionality
bull.b: A sizable BTC treasury (~15.7k BTC, ≈$1.1B) is a non-dilutive liquidity source management uses for disciplined sales to fund CapEx and development. Over months this reduces reliance on equity issuance and enables tactical financing or project-backed lending without immediate equity dilution.

Owning ESS Metron and a $193M engineering backlog lowers supply-chain risk, reduces outsourced CapEx and shortens delivery timelines. Increased internal engineering capacity and documented CapEx savings improve repeatable development economics and support scalable, faster data-center rollouts.

bear.t: Negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow forces reliance on asset sales, credit facilities or external financing to fund growth. Over a multi‑month horizon this constrains capital flexibility, raises funding cost and heightens execution risk if cash generation doesn't improve.

Large non‑cash BTC revaluations drive outsized GAAP swings that obscure operating performance, complicate covenant assessment and investor evaluation. Persistent accounting volatility can impair credit terms, planning and market confidence over medium-term horizons.

bear.t: Early-stage data center revenue is low-margin
bear.b: With most data-center revenue currently low-margin fit-outs and minimal recurring operating-lease income, margin expansion depends on successful conversion to long‑term leases. Until recurring high‑margin leases scale, profitability and cash generation will remain pressured despite top-line growth.
